claims.text: Kustomize customizes plain Kubernetes YAML without templates: a kustomization.yaml lists resources and transformations, and kubectl has Kustomize built in, so kubectl kustomize <dir> prints the built manifests to standard output.
claims.source_hint: kubectl.docs.kubernetes.io: Guides > Introduction > Kustomize; kubectl reference: kubectl kustomize

claims.text: kubectl kustomize prints what a kustomization directory builds and applies nothing; applying is a separate step (kubectl apply -k).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Manage Kubernetes objects > Declarative management using Kustomize (kubectl kustomize to view, kubectl apply -k to apply); kubectl reference: kubectl kustomize

claims.text: An entry under resources may be a directory containing its own kustomization.yaml (here ../../base); Kustomize builds it first and the overlay's patches, images and generators apply to the result.
claims.source_hint: kubectl.docs.kubernetes.io: Reference > kustomization > resources; Guides > Bases and Overlays

claims.text: A patch target selects one or several objects (here kind Deployment, name api); a patch may be a list of operations with op, path, value (one of the patch forms). path /spec/replicas is replicas under spec; replace changes only that field, the rest comes from the base.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Declarative management using Kustomize > patches (target selector; strategic merge and JSON6902 forms)

claims.text: The images field matches containers by image name across the built output and sets newTag and digest for every match; the api Deployment and the migration hook each get theirs from a separate entry in the same images field.
claims.source_hint: kubectl.docs.kubernetes.io: Reference > kustomization > images (name, newTag, digest)

claims.text: configMapGenerator creates a ConfigMap whose name gets a suffix hashed from its content, and Kustomize rewrites references to it in other objects (such as envFrom configMapRef) to the suffixed name.
A changed generator value gives a new ConfigMap name; the Deployment's Pod template then changes, which starts a rolling update of its Pods.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io docs: Concepts > Workloads > Deployments (rollout triggered only by .spec.template change); base/kustomization.yaml comment lines 30-33

claims.text: Kustomize can turn off the name suffix hash (generatorOptions.disableNameSuffixHash); then a changed value updates the ConfigMap in place and no Pod restarts.
claims.source_hint: kubectl.docs.kubernetes.io: Reference > kustomization > generatorOptions; kubernetes.io: Configure a Pod to Use a ConfigMap (env vars not updated)

claims.text: At stage-3, base/kustomization.yaml lists every manifest and has configMapGenerator api whose literals are NAME=value lines incl. OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true; base/api.yaml: replicas: 2, untagged image ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api, envFrom configMapRef api.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/gitops/config-repo-kustomize/base/kustomization.yaml lines 34-43, base/api.yaml lines 15, 33-38 at stage-3

claims.text: envs/staging lists ../../base, seven sealed-*.yaml files and images for six images; envs/production lists ../../base, a patch setting the api's replicas to 3 and the same images.

kustomize-render.sh copies the layout to a temp folder with empty files for the SealedSecrets; both overlays build 41 objects; staging's api ConfigMap name appears twice; the diff is one changed line (445c445), replicas 2 vs 3.
At stage-3, envs/production holds a single file, kustomization.yaml; the recorded output shows ... in place of the hash.
Try it: rendering envs/production prints name: api-egress once and name: api-<suffix> twice; changing OTEL_SDK_DISABLED in the base's literals changes the suffix; nothing is applied.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 2, 6 and kustomize-render.txt (production lists only ../../base, no sealed files needed); run locally to confirm

beyond_scope: mentions that the hash suffix can be turned off (misconception 3), without naming the option
